questions.question:
Selecting from the given alternatives, fill in the blank in the following sentence with the correct idiom with the meaning 'to come into the possession of someone undesirable such as an opponent or a competitor'.
Do not disclose your weaknesses to anyone as it may ____.

options.text: wound up in the right hands
end up in the right ends
wind up in the wrong hands
mend up in the odd hands

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**wind up in the wrong hands**'.

 

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom '**wind up in the wrong hands**' (or fall into the wrong hands) means to come into the **possession** of someone who is **undesirable**, such as an **opponent**, a **competitor**, or someone who might use the information for **harmful purposes**.
 
• In the given sentence, the speaker is warning against disclosing **weaknesses** because that information could be used by **enemies** or **rivals** against the person.
 
• The phrasal verb '**wind up**' means to reach or come to a certain place, situation, or condition, often **unexpectedly**.

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 3**'.

**Complete Sentence:** *Do not disclose your weaknesses to anyone as it may **wind up in the wrong hands**__.*

**__Additional Information__**

 
• '**In the right hands**': This means being in the care or possession of someone **competent**, **trustworthy**, or **reliable**.
 
• The phrases '**right ends**' and '**odd hands**' are not standard **idiomatic expressions** in the English language and do not fit the semantic requirements of the sentence.
 
• The warning context of the sentence ('Do not disclose...') requires a **negative outcome**, making 'wrong hands' the only logical choice.
</ul

questions.question: Choose the word that is the closest synonym to the word "guard".
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Defend**.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **'guard'** means to watch over in order to protect or control, or to keep watch over a person or place to prevent a loss or escape. (रक्षा करना / पहरा देना)
 
 
• **Example:** The security officer was hired to **guard** the private property and ensure no unauthorized entry.
 
 
 
• **'Defend'** refers to the act of resisting an attack made on someone or something, or protecting someone or something from harm or danger. (बचाव करना / रक्षा करना)
 
 
• **Example:** It is the duty of the national army to **defend** the country from any external threats.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the closest synonym of **'guard'** is **'defend'** as both words involve the concept of protection.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Defend**.

**Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Attack** (आक्रमण करना): To take aggressive action against someone or something with weapons or armed force.
 
 
• **Example:** The general ordered his troops to **attack** the enemy base at dawn.
 
 
 
• **Discard** (निकाल देना / त्यागना): To get rid of someone or something as no longer useful or desirable.
 
 
• **Example:** You should **discard** any items in the refrigerator that have passed their expiration date.
 
 
 
• **Abandon** (छोड़ देना / परित्याग करना): To cease to support or look after someone; to desert or leave a place or thing permanently.
 
 
• **Example:** The sailors were forced to **abandon** the ship when it started to sink rapidly.

questions.question:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into Passive Voice?
Had she sent invitation cards to all the guests on Monday?

options.text: Had invitation cards been sent by her to all the guests on Monday?
Have invitation cards been sent by her to all the guests on Monday?
Were invitation cards sent by her to all the guests on Monday?
Were all the guests send invitation cards by her on Monday?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Had invitation cards been sent by her to all the guests on Monday?**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The original sentence is an **interrogative sentence** in the **Past Perfect Tense**, which follows the active voice structure: **Had + Subject + V3 (Past Participle) + Object + ?**.

• To convert a **Past Perfect** question into **Passive Voice**, the structure changes to: **Had + Object (New Subject) + been + V3 + by + Agent + ?**.

• In this transformation, the direct object **invitation cards** moves to the subject position, while the auxiliary verb **Had** remains at the beginning to maintain the **question format**.

• The word **been** is introduced as the **passive auxiliary** required for perfect tenses to denote that the action was performed upon the object.

• The main verb **sent** is already in its **past participle (V3)** form, so it remains unchanged in the passive construction.

• The active subject **she** is converted into its objective pronoun form **her** and is preceded by the preposition **by** to indicate the **agent** of the action.

• The additional phrase **to all the guests on Monday** remains intact as it specifies the **recipients** and the **timeframe** of the completed action.

 **Additional Information__**

• Comparison with incorrect tense forms:

• **Present Perfect Tense**: Option 2 uses **Have**. In passive voice, Present Perfect uses **Has/Have + been + V3**, which is incorrect here as the original sentence is in the past.

• **Simple Past Tense**: Option 3 uses **Were**. The **Simple Past** passive structure is **Was/Were + V3**. This is incorrect because it fails to capture the **perfective aspect** (completed action in the past) indicated by **Had**.

• **Grammatical Consistency**: Option 4 uses the auxiliary **Were** combined with the base verb **send**. Passive voice **always** requires the **Past Participle** form (sent), making this option grammatically invalid.

</ul

questions.question:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into active voice?
The annual award ceremony was attended by hundreds of distinguished guests from different countries.

options.text: Hundreds of distinguished guests from different countries attend the annual award ceremony.
Hundreds of distinguished guests from different countries attended the annual award ceremony.
Hundreds of distinguished guests from different countries are attending the annual award ceremony.
Hundreds of distinguished guests from different countries will attend the annual award ceremony.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hundreds of distinguished guests from different countries attended the annual award ceremony**__.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The original sentence is in the **Passive Voice**. This is identified by the structure **Subject (The annual award ceremony) + was + Past Participle (attended) + by + Agent (hundreds of distinguished guests...)**.
 
• In **Active Voice**, the **agent** of the action becomes the **subject**. Therefore, **Hundreds of distinguished guests from different countries** must lead the sentence.
 
• The tense of the sentence must be preserved during conversion. The phrase **was attended** is in the **Simple Past Tense**. The corresponding active form is the simple past verb **attended**.
 
• The receiver of the action in the passive sentence (**The annual award ceremony**) functions as the **direct object** in the active sentence.
 
• Combining these elements, the structure becomes: **Subject + V2 (attended) + Object**. Hence, the second option is the logically and grammatically correct conversion.

 **Additional Information__**

 
• Understanding **Voice** and **Tense** consistency:
 
 
• **Simple Present Tense**: If the active verb is **attend/attends**, the passive form becomes **is/am/are attended**.
 
• **Present Continuous Tense**: If the active verb is **are attending**, the passive form becomes **is/are being attended**.
 
• **Simple Future Tense**: If the active verb is **will attend**, the passive form becomes **will be attended**.
 
• **Simple Past Tense**: The active verb **attended** matches the passive **was/were attended**, which is the specific case in this question.
 
 
 
• The phrase **from different countries** acts as an **adjective phrase** modifying the noun **guests** and must remain attached to it to maintain the original meaning.
</ul

questions.question:
A part of the following sentence is underlined. Choose the option that can replace the underlined part to improve the sentence. If you feel Options A, B, or C do not improve the sentence, then choose Option D: "No improvement required."
He studied all night for the exam but failed to remember nothing the next day.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**failed to remember anything**__.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The original sentence contains a **double negative** error. In English grammar, using two negative words in the same clause typically results in a positive meaning, which contradicts the intended context of the sentence.
 
• The verb **failed** already carries a negative implication (the inability to achieve an action). Pairing it with the negative pronoun **nothing** creates a logical fallacy suggesting the subject remembered something.
 
• To express a total lack of recall, the negative verb must be followed by the **non-assertive** indefinite pronoun **anything**. This structure maintains the negative sense required by the conjunction **but**, which indicates a contrast between studying all night and the poor outcome.
 
• Grammatically, **failed to remember anything** is equivalent to the phrase **remembered nothing**. However, since **failed** is already part of the sentence structure, **anything** is the only appropriate choice to complete the thought logically.

 **Additional Information__**

 
• **Usage of Indefinite Pronouns:**
 
 
• **Anything:** This is an **indefinite pronoun** used primarily in **negative sentences**, questions, and conditional clauses. It serves as the counterpart to **something** in non-affirmative contexts.
 
• **Nothing:** This is used in affirmative sentences to give them a negative meaning (e.g., 'I have nothing'). Combining it with words like **failed**, **without**, or **scarcely** is a common stylistic error.
 
 
 
• **Contextual Logic of Other Options:**
 
 
• **Failed to forget everything:** This would logically imply that the person managed to remember everything, which is semantically opposite to the failure suggested by the context of a difficult exam situation.
 
• **Failed to forget anything:** This suggests a **perfect memory** or total recall, which does not align with the narrative of struggling after a long night of study.
 
 
</ul
